newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV's Privanza '97 funds seen rising to 900 bln.
newsitem.headline: BBV's Privanza '97 funds seen rising to 900 bln.

text.p: Funds under management at the Privanza private banking unit of Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya could rise to between 900 and 950 billion pesetas, a top official of the unit said on Tuesday.

"We have surpassed our estimates. Extrapolating, Privanza funds under management could rise to 900 to 950 billion. If we don't get to one trillion by the end of the year, it will be soon," Privanza vice general director Carlos Zumalacaregui told journalists at a presentation.
The group currently manages 850 billion in funds, up 28.5 percent from end-June 1996.
Pre-tax profits through May rose 58.8 percent to 1.25 billion pesetas. Privanza estimates pre-tax profits for the year will reach three billion from 2.02 billion in 1996.

Privanza, whose name is being changed to BBV Privanza to reflect its strategic importance to the group, is Spain's leading private banking group, according to an independent study, and had a 16.9 percent market share at end-1995.
Unlike rival Banco Central Hispano, which last week announced a global private banking deal with British merchant bank Rothschild, BBV is pursuing this market segment on its own.
"This is a strategic business for BBV and we do not like to open it up to anyone. We believe we can do it and we are doing it on our own," Privanza chairman Eduardo de Aguirre Alonso-Allende said.
In Latin America, traditionally a strong area for private banking, BBV is marketing its products through its extensive network of new financial holdings.
